teaser.text: Synopsys sells the software, reusable circuit designs, testing hardware and engineering help that turn chip ideas into products. Its customers pay for progress and confidence, while Synopsys spends to keep a complicated design system useful.

stock.title: Synopsys stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Synopsys stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash generation, risks and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: Synopsys's weighted forecast reaches $790.14 by October 2029, a 69% gain. It hinges on turning acquisition-led growth into durable cash per share.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Synopsys's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is slightly negative after one year but strongly positive after three. The shares reach $459.78 in October 2027, a 2% loss including dividends. They reach $648.73 in October 2028, a 39% gain. By October 2029, the weighted value is $790.14, a 69% gain.

blocks.heading: What could make Synopsys's stock forecast work or fail?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes China restrictions disrupt design starts and local tools take share. AI and IP agreements fail to convert into repeat paid activity, while Ansys cross-selling remains slow and integration costs persist. The shares reach $259.87 in October 2027. They reach $412.42 in October 2029, with 27% probability because cash conversion, debt service and dilution could all weaken together.

The bull case requires several conversions at once. Customers repeatedly adopt combined Synopsys–Ansys workflows, AI usage becomes paid capacity, and IP agreements reach production and royalties. Strong cash conversion funds debt reduction and buybacks. The shares reach $682.26 in October 2027. They reach $1,304.26 in October 2029, with 20% probability because the evidence shows technical wins but not yet recurring incremental cash.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Synopsys really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation adds another qualification. Synopsys recorded $712.6 million of it in the first nine months of FY2026. Operating cash flow adds that non-cash expense back, but shareholders may pay through dilution. A specialist therefore asks whether cash grows per share, not merely whether the cash-flow statement looks strong.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Synopsys today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings, compares the share price with forecast earnings per share. At 25.1 times, investors pay $25.10 for each dollar of expected earnings. Management’s FY2027 target shows why the definition matters: the GAAP operating margin is 20.7%, while the adjusted margin is 44.0%. The difference includes amortization, which spreads an acquisition’s cost over time, and stock compensation, which pays employees with ownership claims. The first is non-cash in the current year; the second can dilute shareholders.

blocks.heading: What has Synopsys guided for FY2027?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to a 69% gain by October 2029, hinged on rising cash generation, debt reduction and durable adoption of Synopsys–Ansys, AI and IP products. Management’s FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $11,100–$11,200 million. It calls for non-GAAP operating margin of 44.0% and the company’s own free cash flow of $3,100 million. Through FY2030, its framework targets roughly 15% annual revenue growth and roughly 50% adjusted operating margin. Stock compensation, debt service and integration work still absorb cash.

blocks.heading: Has Synopsys kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: A performance restricted stock unit is a promise of shares that pays only if specified results are achieved. The 2023–2025 award paid nothing because certified revenue growth was 10.3%, below its 13.0% goal. The next award excludes more than US$100 million of revenue per acquisition, so buying Ansys cannot automatically satisfy the growth test. That protects against rewarding purchased revenue, but shareholders must still judge whether management creates value by integrating the acquisition.

blocks.heading: How have Synopsys revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The same distinction appears in Q3 FY2026. Total revenue grew about 42%, but EDA, or electronic design automation, grew 8.5%, while Design IP grew about 11%. It is like a grocery chain buying another store: combined sales rise immediately, even if the original store attracts no more shoppers.

GAAP operating margin was 14.4%, while the company’s adjusted margin was 41.6%. GAAP diluted EPS rose to $2.84 from $1.50, while adjusted EPS rose to $3.91 from $3.39. The difference reflects excluded expenses and the Processor IP disposal gain. A larger share count also means total profit does not flow through proportionately to each share.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Synopsys results?

paragraphs.text: The decisive evidence will be customers using the new products repeatedly while Synopsys meets its cash and debt commitments.
